newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Health Ministry approves HIV gene therapy.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Health Ministry approves HIV gene therapy.

text.p: Japan's Health Ministry said on Monday it gave the go-ahead on May 30 for research on gene therapy to be conducted on patients with HIV, the virus that causes AIDS.
The research will be conducted at Kumamoto University in southern Japan and will be sponsored by Osaka-based drug maker Green Cross Corp, the ministry said.
Green Cross said earlier it would use an anti-HIV gene therapy product, HIV-IT(V), now under development by a division of U.S.-based Chiron Corp, in research on the new treatment.
Japanese media reports said the research is expected to begin as early as July.
